title: Witness and Cipher
premise: When a water-damaged diary surfaces in the flooded basement of the Winterbourne Hotel, concierge Rosalind Winterbourne recognizes the handwriting of Marguerite Ashe, a guest who vanished twenty years ago — and realizes the entries continue for three days after the date Marguerite was declared dead. As Rosalind deciphers the coded final entries, she discovers the diary implicates her own late father, the hotel's beloved former owner, and that someone in town has been quietly erasing evidence ever since. With the statute of limitations expiring in six weeks, Rosalind must trade her role as keeper of secrets for that of witness, allying with the one man she swore never to trust: Detective Idris Kane, who once accused her of lying to protect the family name. In the end, Rosalind exposes the true killer — the town's retired sheriff, who has been living under the hotel as its maintenance man — and chooses love and belonging over the inherited duty of silence, reopening the hotel not as a vault of secrets but as a home.
about_author: Jonah Oyelaran is a former night-desk clerk at a coastal grand hotel who spent a decade collecting the stories guests left behind in ledgers and lost-and-found boxes. He writes mysteries about the people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She catalogs a storm-damaged hotel basement, introducing her habit of noticing everything and filing it away. She finds a water-swollen diary wedged behind a pipe. Emotional beat: quiet pride in her orderliness, undercut by a flicker of dread at the name on the flyleaf.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Room 214
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She confirms the diary belonged to Marguerite Ashe, the guest who vanished twenty years ago, presumed drowned. The last dated entry is three days after the disappearance. Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into personal obsession.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Polite Silence
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, with a flashback to the night Marguerite vanished and young Rosalind's first lesson in keeping the family's secrets. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited silence pressing down for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Man Who Accused Her
chapters.summary: Detective Idris Kane's POV. Now a private investigator, Kane is back in town for his mother's funeral. He remembers the case he was forced to close — and the concierge whose testimony he never believed. Emotional beat: old resentment tangled with unfinished respect.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The final entries are written in a substitution cipher keyed to the hotel's old room-numbering system — something only a longtime employee could crack. Emotional beat: the thrill of competence becoming the terror of knowing.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Retirement
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. He pays a courtesy call on retired Sheriff Amos Pell, now the hotel's maintenance man, and notices Pell's unease at the word 'basement.' Emotional beat: a detective's instinct reawakening after years of dormancy.

chapters.title: What the Guest Book Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She cross-references the diary against the hotel's guest books and finds a page razored out — dated the night Marguerite disappeared. Emotional beat: betrayal; her own archive has been violated.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Keys
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her father's will gave her the hotel and one instruction: 'keep the books honest.' She realizes the instruction may have meant something else entirely. Emotional beat: love for a dead father curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Six Weeks
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. He learns the statute of limitations on the related obstruction charges expires in six weeks, after which evidence becomes legally worthless. He approaches Rosalind with an uneasy truce. Emotional beat: two adversaries forced into the same corner.

chapters.title: Room 214, Sealed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She and Kane open the long-sealed Room 214 and find the furniture rearranged — someone has been using it, recently. Emotional beat: the past is not past; it is occupied.

chapters.title: The Diary's Second Hand
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Forensic comparison shows the final cipher entries were written by a different hand copying Marguerite's style. The diary is both evidence and forgery — a message meant to be found. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under both of them.

chapters.title: Duty, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her aunt Delphine, the family matriarch, warns her to burn the diary and protect the hotel's name, invoking the Winterbourne duty of discretion. Emotional beat: the theme of duty made flesh, and refused.

chapters.title: The Night Clerk's Confession
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A former night clerk, dying and unafraid, admits he saw Pell carry a heavy carpet bag to the basement twenty years ago — and was paid to forget. Emotional beat: grief for a town complicit in its own silence.

chapters.title: A Love That Filed Itself Away
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Kane, alternating. Working late over the cipher, old attraction resurfaces; both retreat into duty. Emotional beat: tenderness deferred, duty used as armor.

chapters.title: The Cipher's First Word
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She cracks the cipher's key: it spells her father's name. The forger knew him intimately. Emotional beat: vertigo — the conspiracy reaches into her own house.

chapters.title: Delphine's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. He discovers Aunt Delphine has been quietly paying an anonymous account for twenty years — hush money, or penance. Emotional beat: suspicion turning toward the family Rosalind is trying to save.

chapters.title: The Basement Floods Again
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A 'burst pipe' nearly destroys the remaining evidence; she saves the diary by minutes and realizes it was deliberate. Someone is inside the hotel. Emotional beat: fear arriving at her own threshold.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Last Guest
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Records show Marguerite checked in under a false name the night she vanished — she was hiding from someone, not running to someone. Emotional beat: the victim rewritten as a fugitive.

chapters.title: The Statute's Shadow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Four weeks remain. She goes public just enough — a discreet inquiry to the county clerk — and the town's polite machinery begins closing ranks against her. Emotional beat: belonging revoked in real time.

chapters.title: What Pell Knows
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. He confronts Pell obliquely; the maintenance man quotes the hotel's fire-safety routes with unsettling precision — including a tunnel no blueprint shows. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing the quarry built the maze.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Beneath the Winterbourne
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Kane, alternating. They find the tunnel from her father's Prohibition-era blueprints and, at its end, a locked room with Marguerite's belongings — and a second diary, in her true hand. Emotional beat: awe and horror; the missing woman lived here, hidden.

chapters.title: Alive Until She Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The true diary reveals Marguerite hid in the hotel for three days after her 'disappearance,' protected by someone she called 'W.' — her father. Then the entries stop mid-sentence. Emotional beat: hope and grief in the same breath.

chapters.title: Delphine, Cornered
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Delphine confesses the hush money: she has been paying Marguerite's daughter, raised in secret, believing the Winterbournes owed a debt of silence. Emotional beat: duty revealed as love wearing duty's uniform.

chapters.title: The Daughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She meets Nell Ashe, the daughter, a hotel housekeeper at a rival property — placed there, it turns out, by someone watching the family. Emotional beat: kinship with a stranger who shares her inheritance of secrets.

chapters.title: Two Weeks
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. With the statute expiring, Kane files what they have; the DA balks without a body or a confession. Emotional beat: the law's limits against the truth's stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Forger's Mistake
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The cipher forgery uses a room-numbering system that only changed after Marguerite vanished — so the forger learned the hotel after 2005. Only three people fit. Emotional beat: the net tightening, and her own name briefly inside it.

chapters.title: The Fire Alarm
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A midnight fire alarm empties the hotel; in the chaos, the true diary is stolen from her office. Emotional beat: violation, and the cold clarity of knowing exactly who had access.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty, Stated Plainly
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Kane. On the fire escape, Kane offers to walk away with her when this ends; she admits she has never belonged anywhere but the hotel — and that belonging is the trap. Emotional beat: the love theme declared, unresolved.

chapters.title: The Trap in Room 214
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. They stage a fake discovery in Room 214 and watch. Pell takes the bait, entering the sealed room through the tunnel. Emotional beat: the pivot from pursued to hunters.

chapters.title: Confession in the Dark
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Trapped by his own tunnel, Pell confesses: he killed Marguerite when she discovered he'd been selling guest information, then staged the drowning — but her father hid her body to protect the hotel, and the forger used the cipher to force the truth out. Emotional beat: the case cracking open, one confession short of complete.

chapters.title: The Forger Revealed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The cipher's key — her father's name — was chosen by Delphine, who forged the diary to finally force someone to dig, unable to confess herself. Emotional beat: fury dissolving into sorrow for a woman who weaponized truth because she couldn't speak it.

chapters.title: Where Marguerite Lies
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Kane. Following her father's ledger notation — 'the honest books' — they find Marguerite's remains in the old wine cellar behind a false wall. Emotional beat: the case closing with grief, not triumph.

chapters.title: The Statute Expires
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Pell is arrested for murder — the statute never applied to it; the deadline was a red herring Delphine used as a spur. Emotional beat: bitter relief; the law was never the obstacle, silence was.

chapters.title: Nell's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind gives Nell her mother's recovered diary and a standing room at the hotel. Emotional beat: belonging offered where duty once demanded silence.

chapters.title: Delphine's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Delphine, facing charges for evidence tampering, asks Rosalind to keep the family name intact one last time. Rosalind refuses — gently. Emotional beat: the theme resolved; love without duty's leash.

chapters.title: The Guest Book, Restored
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She reconstructs the razored page from her twenty years of notes and files it in the archive — truth, alphabetized at last. Emotional beat: her gift of noticing finally turned from keeping secrets to keeping witness.

chapters.title: Kane's Decision
chapters.summary: Kane's POV. Offered his old detective's badge back, he declines and instead signs on as the hotel's security consultant — a man choosing a place over a career. Emotional beat: duty redirected toward home.

chapters.title: Room 214, Open
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She reopens Room 214 as a ordinary guest suite, Marguerite's name restored to the hotel's honor roll. Emotional beat: exorcism by hospitality; the past given a kind room instead of a locked one.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She begins her own diary, first line echoing Marguerite's: 'If you are reading this, someone finally noticed.' Emotional beat: the witness becoming the inheritance.

chapters.title: Witness and Cipher
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Kane, closing scene at the front desk on a stormy night, a new guest checking in. She notices everything — and now tells what she knows. Emotional beat: peace earned, love chosen, the hotel a home rather than a vault.
